headline: Record full year, but a softer fourth-quarter profit dip
summary_short: Fiscal Q4 revenue rose 4.7% to $644M but diluted EPS fell 10.2% to $1.57 as operating income dropped 12.2% on higher personnel and amortization costs; full-year diluted EPS still grew 11.9% to $6.98 on record revenue of $2.54B.
summary_long: Jack Henry closed fiscal 2026 with a record year but a bumpier Q4. Fourth-quarter revenue grew 4.7% to $644M (non-GAAP adjusted revenue +6.6%), but operating income fell 12.2% to $137M and diluted EPS dropped 10.2% to $1.57, driven by higher personnel, compensation, and capitalized-software amortization costs outpacing revenue growth. Full-year revenue reached $2.54B (+7.1%), operating income $635M (+11.7%), and diluted EPS $6.98 (+11.9%), with free cash flow up 31.4% to $539M and ROIC of 23.2%. The company drew down cash to $12M (from $102M) while adding $40M of borrowings, funding $448M of full-year buybacks. Jack Henry initiated FY2027 guidance of $2.68-2.71B GAAP revenue and $7.33-7.38 diluted EPS, implying 5.5-6.5% revenue growth.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by cloud hosting (+7.4%), license/hardware (+27.3%), card revenue (+5.4%), digital transaction revenue (+8.6%), and faster payments (+47.0%), partly offset by lower deconversion revenue.
Cost of revenue, R&D, and SG&A all grew faster than revenue, due to higher personnel and compensation costs tied to headcount growth plus increased amortization of capitalized software.
Follows lower net income (-12.8% y/y) on higher operating expenses, only partly offset by a smaller diluted share count from buybacks.

CEO cited record 58 competitive core wins in fiscal 2026, including 14 institutions over $1B in assets, and record non-GAAP revenue; CFO flagged FY2027 margin comparisons will be tougher versus H1 FY2026.
